headline: Record revenue and profit growth as AI demand surges
summary_short: Cisco reported record quarterly revenue of $15.84B, up 12% y/y, with GAAP EPS of $0.85 (+37% y/y) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.06 (+10% y/y), exceeding the high end of its own guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 12% y/y to $15.84B; GAAP EPS rose to $0.85 (+37%) and non-GAAP EPS to $1.06 (+10%), exceeding the high end of Cisco's own guidance. Growth was driven by 17% product-revenue growth (Networking +25%) against a 1% services decline; Americas +14%, EMEA +9%, APJC +9%. GAAP gross margin fell to 63.6% from 65.6%, while GAAP operating margin expanded to 25.0% from about 22.6% as revenue outpaced a 1% rise in opex. Product orders rose 35% y/y, with AI infrastructure orders at $5.3B year-to-date. Cash and investments were $16.6B; Cisco returned $2.9B to shareholders. Q4 FY2026 guidance: revenue $16.7-16.9B, non-GAAP EPS $1.16-1.18; FY2026 AI-infrastructure revenue outlook raised to $4B from $3B.

drivers.explanation: Product revenue grew 17% y/y (Networking +25%) while services revenue fell 1%; by geography Americas +14%, EMEA +9%, APJC +9%.
Gross profit grew as revenue rose 12%, but margin compressed since cost of sales grew faster (+18%) than revenue; the release states no specific cause for the compression.
Operating margin expanded to 25.0% from about 22.6% because GAAP opex rose only 1% while revenue grew 12%, per the release's own disclosed opex figures.
Net income growth also reflects a swing to $242M of other income from a $102M loss a year ago, alongside the operating-income gain.
CEO cited broad-based AI-and-security-driven demand; CFO cited double-digit top/bottom-line growth exceeding the high end of guidance and record non-GAAP operating income.
